title: Hummingbird: A Smaller and Faster Large Language Model Accelerator on Embedded FPGA
problem: Deploying LLMs on embedded FPGAs faces severe constraints: limited on-chip/off-chip memory (4GB barrier), high resource consumption, and insufficient prior exploration of embedded FPGA potential for LLM inference compared to cloud-grade FPGA solutions.
motivation: Edge deployment of LLMs is critical for privacy, latency, and cost optimization; existing solutions require expensive cloud-grade hardware and support only small models.
method: Hummingbird employs memory-offloading strategies to overcome 4GB embedded FPGA memory constraints and scales to 8B-parameter LLMs. The design optimizes DSP/LUT/power utilization through architecture refinement targeting KV260/ZCU104 embedded FPGAs, achieving 93-94% model bandwidth utilization.
key_novelty: First practical FPGA accelerator supporting LLaMA3-8B inference on resource-constrained embedded FPGAs through intelligent memory offloading.
contributions: 67% LUT, 39% DSP, 42% power savings vs. existing embedded FPGA LLM accelerators
4.8 tokens/s on KV260, 8.6 tokens/s on ZCU104 for LLaMA3-8B
Extended context support through memory offloading strategy
limitations: Limited to embedded FPGA platforms (KV260, ZCU104); evaluation focused on LLaMA variants; Spartan deployment mentioned but not thoroughly evaluated.
primary_theme: Edge LLM inference on embedded FPGAs
